Contributing to spDBL

Source: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md

Thank you for considering a contribution. This guide covers reporting problems, setting up a development copy, and the checks a change should pass. Please follow the Code of Conduct in all project spaces.

Reporting bugs and asking questions

Ask usage questions, and share how you use spDBL, in GitHub Discussions. Report bugs at https://github.com/xiangchen-stat/spDBL/issues. A minimal reproducible example (reprex::reprex()) and your sessionInfo() make it much easier to help. For calibration problems, include the rstan and StanHeaders versions and your compiler.

Before a larger change

For a new feature, model component, or change to an exported function, please open an issue first so we can agree on the design. Small fixes (typos, documentation, clear bugs) can go straight to a pull request.

The architecture article (vignettes/articles/architecture.Rmd) maps each workflow function to the code that implements it and lists the main extension points.

Development setup

You need R (≥ 4.0), a C++ compiler for the Rcpp/RcppEigen code, and, for calibration work, rstan.

# install.packages(c("pak", "devtools"))
pak::local_install_dev_deps()   # from the package root; installs Imports and Suggests
devtools::load_all()            # compile and load the development version

Making a change

  1. Create a branch from main.
  2. Edit the code. Documentation lives in roxygen comments next to each function; run devtools::document() to regenerate man/ and NAMESPACE. Never edit man/*.Rd or NAMESPACE by hand.
  3. Add or update tests (see below).
  4. Add a bullet to NEWS.md under the development version.
  5. Run devtools::check(). It should finish with no errors or warnings.
  6. Open a pull request; the checklist in the template repeats these steps.

Conventions

  • License header. Every new R, C++, Stan, or shell file starts with

    # Copyright (c) 2026 Xiang Chen. Part of the spDBL R package.
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

    (use // in C++ and Stan files). bash .github/scripts/check-license-headers.sh checks this, and so does CI.

  • Names. New functions use snake_case. Kernel functions follow the covariance-model suffixes: none for inverse-Wishart, _sigma2R, and _I. Some older exported names (generate.grid.*) are kept for compatibility.

  • Randomness. Functions that take a seed set it locally and restore the caller’s random-number state on exit; reuse the internal .cal_seed() helper for this.

  • Files. Examples, tests, and vignettes must not write outside tempdir(). Plot helpers that can save files (savei = TRUE) need a temporary path in examples and tests.

  • C++. Edit src/*.cpp. devtools::document() runs Rcpp::compileAttributes(), which regenerates R/RcppExports.R and src/RcppExports.cpp; do not edit those two files.

  • Stan. The programs are in inst/stan/. The R functions calibration_log_density() and calibration_marginal_log_density() (in R/calibration_recover.R) are reference implementations of the same densities, and the Stan tests compare them. Change both together.

Tests

Tests are in tests/testthat/ (testthat, 3rd edition).

devtools::test()                        # unit tests; no Stan compilation
Sys.setenv(SPDBL_RUN_STAN_TESTS = "true")
devtools::test()                        # also compile and run the Stan programs

The Stan tests are skipped by default because they need a C++ compiler and are much slower than the unit tests. Set SPDBL_STAN_CACHE_DIR to a directory to keep compiled models between runs.

Prefer tests that compare against an independent calculation (a closed-form posterior, direct Gaussian conditioning, an in-memory version of an out-of-core computation) over tests that only check that code runs. Keep test dimensions small: the default suite runs on CRAN. Mark slow tests with skip_on_cran().

Coverage:

Sys.setenv(SPDBL_RUN_STAN_TESTS = "true")
covr::report(covr::package_coverage())   # opens an HTML report

On every push and pull request, GitHub Actions runs R CMD check on macOS, Windows, and Ubuntu (release and the previous release), measures coverage with the Stan tests on, checks license headers, and rebuilds the website. R CMD check on R-devel runs weekly, and on demand from the Actions tab (R-CMD-check-devel.yaml), because its dependencies compile from source.

Vignettes

The .Rmd files in vignettes/ are the sources. The Quarto copies (.qmd) are generated from them; never edit them directly:

Rscript data-raw/sync-vignettes.R

To render a vignette against the current source rather than an older installed version, run from the package directory:

bash vignettes/renderEmulation.sh quarto calibration

The helper installs the current source into the ignored .r-library directory, then renders calibration.qmd. Omit calibration to render all three vignettes, or use r instead of quarto for R Markdown.

Package builds of the calibration vignette never compile Stan; they show a recorded result. To reproduce it, run the installed script system.file("examples", "run_calibration.R", package = "spDBL"), then record the output with Rscript data-raw/record-calibration.R <output_dir>.

Example data

Scripts in data-raw/ rebuild the shipped data:

  • data-raw/sir-calibration.R builds dt_calibration from saved SIR simulations (pass their directory as the argument).
  • data-raw/record-calibration.R records the calibration vignette’s result.

Website

The website is built with pkgdown from _pkgdown.yml, the README, the help pages, and the vignettes. To preview it locally, run pkgdown::build_site() in a copy of the repository with vignettes/*.qmd (generated duplicates) and vignettes/reproduce/ (research notebooks that need the original simulation data) removed; the GitHub Actions workflow does the same before deploying the site from main.
